root_cause: Exact production and affected-route readback were healthy, but the pricing browser proof produced sequential Playwright locator false negatives: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded timed out, then locator waitFor visible timed out, and after readiness recovery locator.boundingBox timed out for 30 seconds. The canonical HTML/CSS contains exactly one loss-stage control and mobile lifecycle tabs are rendered as a visible grid. The failure class is locator auto-wait/geometry instability, not missing production content. A fourth production readback on exact main 984f679515fff2d9e4a4f10c0b187e95e96a1561 showed locator.evaluate can still auto-wait for 30 seconds even after ready-v3 when the concrete lifecycle control is not yet observable to the locator. The readiness marker alone therefore did not prove that the pointer target itself was present.
prevention_rule: After the product-specific ready-v3 marker, prove actionability from direct DOM computed visibility and getBoundingClientRect geometry. Fail closed for display:none, visibility:hidden, opacity 0 or zero-sized controls. Use page.mouse.click at the measured center to preserve a real pointer interaction. Do not use locator visibility/geometry auto-waits, force:true, or DOM click shortcuts when those auto-waits are the observed failure mode. Couple product readiness to the concrete target: wait until ready-v3 AND document.querySelector('[data-bg-stage="loss"]') are both true, then use page.evaluate with direct DOM lookup for visibility, scrolling and geometry. Never use locator.evaluate for the observed failure class.

failed_runs.failure: locator.evaluate TimeoutError waiting for [data-bg-stage="loss"] after ready-v3

invariants: pricing ready-v3 marker remains the domain-specific readiness authority
genuinely hidden or zero-sized lifecycle controls fail closed
production interaction proof uses direct DOM geometry plus a real page.mouse pointer event
lifecycle selection billing mutation and English-route semantic assertions remain mandatory
ready-v3 is not sufficient alone; the concrete loss lifecycle control must also exist before pointer proof
pricing production verifier does not use locator.evaluate for lifecycle target geometry
